outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Introduction to Scaling Reinforcement Learning for LLMs
outline.description: Reinforcement learning (RL) has rapidly evolved from a niche optimization technique into a pivotal paradigm for scaling the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs). As the field pushes toward ever-larger models, RL has become the primary mechanism through which these systems develop the ability to tackle sophisticated, high-stakes problems. Specifically, through large-scale RL training, language models acquire the capacity to engage in deeper and longer reasoning processes required for competition-level mathematics, advanced programming tasks, and complex logical deduction. outline.description: To understand the advancements introduced by modern reinforcement learning algorithms for large language models, one must first establish a rigorous understanding of the underlying mathematical framework and the evolutionary path of policy optimization methods. This chapter lays the necessary groundwork by defining the formal notation used to describe autoregressive language models as policies, the mechanisms for scoring their outputs, and the specific objectives of two pivotal algorithms: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). outline.description: The fundamental instability plaguing previous reinforcement learning algorithms for large language models, specifically Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), arises from a conceptual mismatch between the granularity of the reward signal and the granularity of the optimization objective. In the context of training language models, the verification process typically assigns a scalar reward score $r(x, y)$ to an entire query-response pair $(x, y)$. This reward reflects the quality of the complete sequence $y$ generated in response to query $x$.
